items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: For instance the bass player, Vernon Alley, a very fine bass player, he became ill. We were someplace in Texas... they gave him the money that he had earned, we had played like maybe four days of that week

ctx.x: It wasn’t the easiest gig in the world, from what I understand.

It wasn’t, no it wasn’t. There were many times when it wasn’t. And the funny thing of it is that my antagonism towards Lionel didn’t come from anything he did to me personally, it was things that they did to other people that you were witness to you know. For instance the bass player, Vernon Alley, a very fine bass player, he became ill. We were someplace in Texas. And the doctor said he had the flu or something and he has to stay in bed for at least a week. And so it was like okay, they gave him the money that…
Were you aspiring to play in a classical situation at that time also?
